relations: If the upper cylinder descends, the coil spring compresses and its turns move closer together.
The spring rests between the two cylinders, so downward pressure on the top block shortens the coil.
As compression increases, the spring resists with upward force against the upper cylinder's underside.
The lower cylinder supports the spring base, keeping it aligned while the top block presses.
